title: What If the Biggest Solar Storm on Record Hit Today?

scenes.text: What if the biggest solar storm on record hit tonight? In 1859 it set telegraph paper on fire.
It reached Earth in about seventeen hours. Telegraph operators got shocks, and auroras glowed as far south as Cuba.
Today the targets are satellites, GPS, radio and power lines. Storms push currents through long cables and can damage huge transformers.
Those transformers are hard to replace, so some blackouts could last years, experts warn.
A 2017 study put a major blackout at up to forty-one billion dollars a day in the United States alone.
Experts estimate storms this big come once every hundred to a thousand years. The last one was 1859.

description:
What if the Carrington solar storm of 1859 hit today?
It set telegraph paper on fire then. Now it could threaten satellites, GPS and power grids.
